name: Pipe joint + leak test

steps.title: Water supply shutoff verified
steps.visual_criteria: Main line valve closed, line depressurized and drained into bucket

steps.title: Square cut and deburred pipe end
steps.visual_criteria: Pipe cut clean at 90 degrees with cutter; inside and outside edges deburred

steps.title: Thread sealing tape or solvent application
steps.visual_criteria: PTFE tape wrapped clockwise 4-6 turns on threads, or uniform solvent cement coat

steps.title: Joint assembly and wrench tightening
steps.visual_criteria: Fitting pushed fully to socket shoulder or hand-tightened plus 1.5 wrench turns

steps.title: Pressure and leak test verification
steps.visual_criteria: Water supply restored, joint wiped dry, tissue paper or dry finger shows no dampness under pressure

scenario_questions.text: Which direction must PTFE Teflon tape be wrapped around male pipe threads?
expected_points: Wrapped clockwise in the direction of the thread
Prevents tape from unraveling when screwing fitting on

scenario_questions.text: How do you detect a slow or micro leak after assembling a pressurized joint?
expected_points: Wipe joint completely dry with cloth
Check with dry tissue paper or look for pressure drop on gauge

scenario_questions.text: What safety precautions do you take before cutting into an existing pipe line?
expected_points: Isolate supply valve and tag it
Open lower tap to relieve trapped water pressure

common_mistakes: Wrapping PTFE tape counter-clockwise causing it to bunch up
Failing to deburr cut edges leading to flow turbulence and clogging
Over-tightening threaded PVC or CPVC fittings causing stress cracks
Re-pressurizing solvent cement joints before cure time elapsed
